correctness.rationale: Direct divisibility gives \(k\mid n\). A divisor injection yields \(A(\sigma(k)-k-1)\le r\). A composite \(k\) has a proper divisor \(h\ge\sqrt{k}\), giving \(n\le r^2\). For prime \(k=p\), the exact identity \((p^{a-1}-1)N+(p^{a+1}-1)(\sigma(N)-N)=r(p-1)\) splits into \(a=1\), \(a\ge2\) with positive proper-divisor sum, and pure prime power: all non-escape forms satisfy \(n\le\max\{r^2,(r-1)^3\}\). For \(r\ge4\), this is \((r-1)^3\). Exhaustive small-offset checking is applied only after a proven bound, and prime cubes \(p^3\) with \(r=p+1\) attain the cubic threshold at infinitely many offsets. The bundled exact-integer verifier checked \(n\le200000\) and \(r\le35\); computation is not an unbounded proof.

originality.rationale: Theorem 5 of Sándor (2022) gives a qualitative finite-exception/prime-family dichotomy for the same equation but supplies neither the exact parameter criterion \(r-1\) prime nor any explicit all-support sharp cubic cutoff. Theorem 4 omits the valid \((k,n)=(2,8)\) solution for \(r=3\). A previously available affine-divisor-sum classification restricted to \(\Omega(n)\le2\) covers the semiprime behavior but does not imply the unrestricted all-support cutoff. Full-text inspection of focal and follow-up works and targeted semantic searches found no equivalently strong coverage; residual risk is unindexed literature.

value.rationale: An all-prime-support, effective polynomial search cutoff is materially stronger than qualitative finite exceptional-set existence. It yields a complete infinitude criterion for every fixed additive offset while allowing unrestricted prime multiplicity, and has a transparent infinite family of sharp extremizers. These features address a natural parameterized divisor-sum Diophantine problem rather than an arbitrary finite slice or mere recomputation of known semiprime families.
